title: Binary Search
prompt: Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target`, return the index of `target` if it exists in `nums`, or `-1` otherwise. Your solution must run in O(log n) time.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order with distinct values
hints: O(log n) on a sorted array is a strong signal to repeatedly halve the search space.
Keep a low and high pointer. Check the middle element — if it's the target, you're done; otherwise discard the half that can't contain it.
Watch the off-by-one: use `low <= high` as the loop condition, and set `mid = low + Math.floor((high - low) / 2)` to avoid overflow habits carried from other languages.

solution.approach: Maintain `low` and `high` bounds over the search space. At each step, compare the middle element to the target: if equal, return its index; if the middle is too small, search the right half; if too large, search the left half. Continue until the bounds cross.
